issues.description: The problem statement's UML and remarks specify Pneumatic.openValve() with no parameters, but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares openValve(int duration). This contradicts the specification and will confuse students about the expected method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic interface signature match the UML and remarks by declaring void openValve() with no parameters (and update the template/solution files accordingly). Alternatively, if a parameter is intended, update the UML and problem text to specify openValve(int duration) consistently.

issues.description: Within the solution repository there is an internal inconsistency: Pneumatic.openValve(int) is declared in the interface, but implementing classes LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster override openValve() with no parameters. This will cause compilation errors and is inconsistent with the solution's own interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure the interface and all implementing classes use the same openValve signature. Preferably change Pneumatic.openValve(int duration) to void openValve() to match the implementing classes and the UML, or update the implementing classes to accept an int parameter if that was intended.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement defines Pneumatic.openValve() with no parameters, but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares openValve(int duration). This mismatch (method name same but different signature) breaks the one-to-one mapping students expect from the UML to the code and will cause confusion and compilation/implementation errors in the subclasses that are expected to implement openValve() without parameters.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Pneumatic.openValve method signature across artifacts. Change the solution's Pneumatic interface to declare openValve() with no parameters and update all implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) to override openValve() without parameters so the code matches the UML and problem statement.
